title: That's What Hamster Says!
summary: Little Hamster does not want to go to Plutzi the Rabbit's preschool. She tries staying home, coming to work with Mama, getting a wagon and a sticker chart, and Mama always answers, "Maybe tomorrow." In the end she goes, announces that she doesn't care, and sits nicely anyway, just because she feels like it. A rhyming story with a fun repeating line to join in, inspired by Dr. Seuss: rhythm, repetition and things getting bigger and bigger.
pages:
The sun in the window is up and smiling away.
"Get up, Hamster!" Mama calls, waiting by the bed today.
But Hamster stays under the blanket, snug as can be,
pokes out just her nose, and says:
"I don't want to go to the rabbit's preschool! Not me!"

At preschool there's a teacher, and she's a rabbit, you see.
Her name is Plutzi. Plutzi the Rabbit, that's she!
With ears so long they reach the ceiling's height,
and a whistle in her mouth: phwee-phwee! "Sit in a line, nice and tight!"

Mama says, "You're a big girl now, it's true!
And big girls go to preschool, that's what big girls do."
"Then I'm big, and I decide, I'm the boss instead:
I'm staying home! In my pajamas! In bed!"

"At home? Alone?" Mama raised an eyebrow high.
"No, no, and no! That's not a good reply."

"Then I'll come with you to work!" She jumped up from her place.
"I'll sit under your desk, as small as a garlic clove, taking up no space!"
Mama took a deep breath and said, slow and without sorrow:
"Maybe tomorrow."

"Then make me a deal! Buy me a wagon to ride!
A wagon with wheels, with a bell, with a honker on the side!"
Mama took a deep breath and said, slow and without sorrow:
"Maybe tomorrow."

"Then draw me a chart! With stars! With stickers galore!
A hundred gold stars, and a thousand dots, and more!"
"I can't draw you a chart right now, there's no time to borrow.
Maybe tomorrow."

"I don't want to go to the rabbit's preschool! What's not clear?
Either I stay home alone, like a hero right here,
or I come with you to work, the way I say.
Simple! It's clear! Thank you! Okay!"

"At home I love to watch videos all day
on Abba's computer, hidden in the pillows and sheets where it lay.
And then French fries! With lots of ketchup on top!
Crunch, crunch, crunch! And again, and again, and don't stop!"

But in the end, yes, yes, well, in the end, I'll admit,
Hamster went to preschool. With a backpack. And a grumpy face to fit.

She marched into preschool, crossed her arms, and said, "Enough!
I don't care! I'll be as cheeky as I like, so tough!"

Plutzi whistled: phwee-phwee! "Sit nicely in your place,
or you won't get the Shabbat treat today, just in case!
Do you want to miss out too? Do you, my dear?"
asked Plutzi the Rabbit, leaning near.

Hamster was quiet... and quiet... and quiet some more...
Then she sat. Nicely. In her place. Like a doll on the floor.
"I sat because I wanted to, not for a treat, and not because of what you say.
I don't care! That's what Hamster says, okay!"
